name: Michael Bloomberg
role: Mayor of New York City (2002–2013), founder of Bloomberg L.P. and Bloomberg Philanthropies, 2020 Democratic presidential candidate, UN Special Envoy on climate ambition
summary: A technocratic, data-driven centrist Democrat (a former Republican) who pairs strong support for markets and private enterprise with an activist public-health, gun-control, climate and civil-rights agenda. As mayor he banned smoking in workplaces, capped soda sizes, backed congestion pricing, charter schools and marriage equality, and defended stop-question-frisk and counter-terrorism surveillance, later apologizing for stop-and-frisk. In 2020 he ran on a public option, higher taxes on the wealthy, a $15 minimum wage, abortion rights, strict gun laws and rejoining the Paris Agreement, while rejecting Medicare for All, a wealth tax and socialism.

universal-healthcare.rationale: His 2020 health plan states the aim of universal coverage: a Medicare-like public option paid by premiums, with subsidies for people of modest means and an expanded ACA, while letting people keep private insurance. He rejected Medicare for All, so the state guarantees access without providing all coverage itself.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: He called for a $15 federal minimum wage indexed to earnings growth and said of New York's $15 wage that it is 'as it should be nationwide'.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Mixed: he calls himself a big believer in capitalism, rejected throwing it out in the 2020 debate, and in 2026 argued that political ownership of firms destroys market competition and, in 2022, that the private sector is 'the most powerful force we can muster' on climate. His mayoralty and platform also use heavy regulation and public programmes, so he does not state a general preference for markets over governments.

public-ownership.rationale: No position of his own on this statement turned up in his debate answers, 2020 platform, speeches, columns or mayoral record.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: His 2020 plan restores the 39.6% top rate, adds a 5% surtax on income above $5 million (a 44.6% top rate), taxes capital gains above $1 million as ordinary income and raises the corporate rate to 28%; he wrote that he agrees with raising taxes on 'wealthy people like me', though he opposed a wealth tax.

unions-good.rationale: His labor platform says falling union membership has deprived workers of a vital voice for fair wages and protections, and he pledges to strengthen union protections, ban right-to-work laws for private-sector unions and back sectoral bargaining.

property-fundamental.rationale: As mayor his administration pursued the Willets Point redevelopment while reserving eminent domain as a tool, saying it would rather cut deals than condemn (a news report of the record, not his own words).

regulate-corporations.rationale: His financial reform plan promises 'common sense regulation' of banks, a restored and strengthened CFPB, a corporate crime unit at the Justice Department, and rules on payday lending and overdraft fees; his gun plan repeals the industry's liability shield.

cut-welfare.rationale: His 2020 plans expand the Earned Income Tax Credit, guarantee housing vouchers for households below 30% of area median income and widen aid, the opposite of cutting. As mayor he took pride in a falling welfare caseload (2013 State of the City), which the 2020 platform does not repeat.

worker-ownership.rationale: No position of his own on this statement turned up in his debate answers, 2020 platform, speeches, columns or mayoral record.

surveillance-ok.rationale: As mayor he invested 'heavily in our counter-terrorism infrastructure, including a network of cameras', and in April 2013 defended NYPD counter-terrorism intelligence gathering against oversight legislation, warning terrorists might succeed if it undermined that work.

limit-guns.rationale: His platform requires a permit before any gun purchase, universal background checks, a 48-hour wait, an age-21 minimum, red flag laws, an assault weapons and magazine ban and secure storage; he co-founded Mayors Against Illegal Guns and as mayor urged Congress to ban assault weapons and high-capacity magazines, saying this falls within the Second Amendment.
